Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure.
  - Acute dizziness/vertigo described as constant room-spinning for ~2 hours, onset while making breakfast.
  - Associated nausea and shakiness.
- Symptom timeline and progression.
  - Continuous since onset (~2 hours).
  - Prior similar brief episode ~1 month ago lasting 5–10 minutes that resolved spontaneously.
- ENT symptoms (as applicable): throat swelling/closure sensation, voice change, dysphagia/odynophagia, drooling, nasal/ocular symptoms, stridor/noisy breathing, dyspnea, distribution of swelling (lips/tongue/uvula/face), ear/neck symptoms.
  - Ear: Buzzing/tinnitus; denies ear pain and discharge; no subjective hearing loss.
  - Gait unsteady due to vertigo; able to walk.
  - No limb weakness.
  - Fever: Patient does not think so.
  - Recent viral illness: Denied.
  - Other ENT/airway symptoms (throat tightness, voice change, dysphagia/odynophagia, drooling, nasal/ocular symptoms, stridor/noisy breathing, dyspnea, facial/lip/tongue/uvular swelling, neck pain): Not reported.
- Relevant past episodes and treatments (including any prior hospital care or injection therapy).
  - Prior brief vertigo episode ~1 month ago; no treatment sought; resolved within minutes.
- Allergies and current medications (mark missing dose/route/frequency as not documented).
  - Allergies: None reported.
  - Medications: Hormone replacement therapy for premature ovarian failure (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Any relevant social context (e.g., accompaniment/supervision).
  - At home; accompaniment not stated.

Objective:
- Observable swelling and distribution (e.g., lips, tongue, uvula, face) if stated.
  - Not reported.
- Airway/breathing descriptors if stated (e.g., stridor, work of breathing).
  - No respiratory symptoms reported.
- Mental status and associated features (e.g., dizziness, syncope) if stated.
  - Alert and coherent; reports dizziness and nausea; no vomiting reported.
- Vitals and examination findings only if mentioned; otherwise note “Not recorded.”
  - Not recorded.
- Presence of another person with the patient (if stated).
  - Not stated.

Assessment:
- Suspected peripheral vestibular disorder; clinician impression documented as “labyrinthitis.”
- Justification: Sudden onset continuous spinning vertigo for ~2 hours with tinnitus and unsteady gait; no focal limb weakness; no ear pain/discharge; no recent viral illness; prior brief similar episode 1 month ago.
- Conflict noted: Patient reports premature ovarian failure; clinician verbally referenced “premature hearing failure” in error.

Plan:
- Immediate actions taken/advised:
  - Prescription sent to Lloyds Pharmacy: medication name not captured—1 tablet three times daily for 10 days (dose/route not documented). Patient advised medication can be taken with or without food.
- Specific instructions provided:
  - Arrange in-person appointment with doctor for otoscopic ear exam, blood pressure measurement, and gait assessment; patient instructed to call support to book this appointment.
- Escalation criteria/red flags:
  - If limb weakness develops, sudden severe headache occurs, or patient becomes violently sick, attend A&E (emergency department).
- Follow-up:
  - In-person review in the next few days as arranged; further management to be determined after examination.

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Vitals (including orthostatics), full neurological exam (including nystagmus characterization, HINTS/Dix-Hallpike), otoscopic findings, hearing assessment.
  - Exact medication name, dose strength, and route not documented.
  - Documentation of hydration advice, activity/driving precautions, stroke risk assessment, migraine history, recent head trauma, and detailed red flag review not recorded.
- Internal conflicts:
  - “Premature ovarian failure” (patient) vs “premature hearing failure” (clinician) — conflict noted as likely misspeak by clinician.
- Transcript quality:
  - Generally clear; some audio gaps/inaudible portions, including the medication name.
